arrival_process.family: homogeneous Poisson process via exponential inter-arrival times
arrival_process.location_sampling: uniform across the ten routing-eligible demand nodes; independent of AEMET hazard

queue.discipline: arrival-order scan: at each event/release/deadline time, dispatch the oldest queued event that has at least one currently free brigade able to arrive before its deadline; repeat until no feasible queued event remains
queue.expiry: queued incident becomes unserved at arrival_time + deadline_min if not dispatched before expiry

potential.busy_resource_position: assigned incident node after its current service
potential.hypothetical_move: candidate brigade release = dispatch_time + road_ETA_to_incident + service_minutes; release position = incident node
potential.note: AEMET classes remain ordinal 1..6; no conversion to incident probabilities

policies.eco_score: severity * response_delay + 0.0005 * emissions_g + 0.05 * distance_km + lambda * (Phi_after - Phi_before)

protocol.claim_scope: exploratory simulator with real frozen road routing and official AEMET spatial hazard; modeled fleet, synthetic arrivals/severity/service/emissions; not operational efficacy
